sources.title: Introducing GPT-4.1 in the API
sources.evidence: April 14, 2025 announcement explicitly launches GPT-4.1, mini and nano in the API. Identifies the GPT-4.1 family, coding and instruction-following focus, image understanding and nominal one-million-token context. It does not disclose production parameter counts or architecture.

sources.title: GPT-4.1 model
sources.evidence: Full official Markdown retrieved. Exact alias defaults to gpt-4.1-2025-04-14. Specifies 1,047,576-token context, text/image inputs, text output, function calling and non-reasoning behavior. Alias and dated snapshot are marked Deprecated. No production size or architecture is supplied.

sources.title: GPT-4.1 Prompting Guide
sources.evidence: April 14, 2025 guide by OpenAI authors explicitly says GPT-4.1 does not produce an internal chain of thought before answering. Separately permits prompted explicit planning. Describes training for agentic tasks and demonstrates function calls using gpt-4.1-2025-04-14; no production parameter count or architectural structure is disclosed.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Full Markdown retrieved. Includes an exact gpt-4.1 request using document.pdf as input_file. Explains that PDF ingestion extracts text and page images and supplies both to the model; PDF is an API document format rather than a distinct native sensory modality.

sources.title: API deprecations
sources.evidence: Full Markdown retrieved. October 14, 2026 notice lists GPT-4.1 snapshot gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 for shutdown January 14, 2027. Deprecated means scheduled retirement, distinct from completed shutdown. This notice does not change the original release date.

sources.title: Introducing gpt-oss
sources.evidence: August 5, 2025 release states gpt-oss were the first open-weight language models since GPT-2. Corroborates the earlier GPT-4.1 release was hosted rather than open weights. Architecture and counts disclosed for gpt-oss are not transferred to GPT-4.1. Initial direct fetch timed out; indexed full article text was subsequently accessible.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Current agreement applies to API access; sections 2.2 and 9.1 grant limited service access and reserve service intellectual property. Used for the descriptive Proprietary classification, not as a checkpoint license or a claim that these January 2026 terms governed the April 2025 launch.

sources.title: Training agents to self-report misbehavior
sources.evidence: March 21, 2026 first-party research describes training GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini separately using public fine-tuning APIs. It does not disclose either production parameter counts or architecture; its linked full paper was checked as well.

sources.title: Training Agents to Self-Report Misbehavior
sources.publisher: Bruce W. Lee, Yueh-Han Chen and Tomek Korbak
sources.evidence: Full 91-page paper downloaded and text-extracted from the link on the OpenAI research article; HTML also inspected. Reviewed GPT-4.1 training/evaluation sections and searched all parameter, architecture and Transformer references. No exact GPT-4.1 production parameter count, broad architecture or dense/MoE routing disclosure was found. Tool-schema parameters and unrelated Transformer citations do not establish model size or structure.

sources.title: OpenAI GPT-5 System Card
sources.evidence: Full paper downloaded and text-extracted from the official GPT-5 system-card page. Searched GPT-4.1, parameter, architecture and Transformer references. The full-size GPT-4.1 mention concerns its April 2025 health-model release chronology; no production count or architecture is provided. The separate GPT-4.1-nano successor table is not evidence about this full-size model.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: February 18, 2026 guide by Erika Kettleson (OpenAI), read in HTML and complete Markdown. Section 2.1 describes OpenAI inference caching through Transformer layers and attention key/value tensors; section 2.2 explicitly includes gpt-4.1. The archived guide applies to models before GPT-5.6. It does not disclose routing subtype, dimensions or parameter counts.

name.note: Exact full-size model, distinct from GPT-4.1 mini and nano.

developer.note: Official OpenAI release and hosted-model documentation identify the developer.

family.note: The original release and guide explicitly name the GPT-4.1 model family; use this specific family rather than generic GPT.

release_date.note: The dated announcement explicitly launches public API access that day. Later ChatGPT availability and the October 2026 deprecation are separate lifecycle events.

open_weights.note: Released through the hosted API. First-party open-weight release history corroborates that this GPT-4.1 release did not distribute weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the closed hosted model, not a named downloadable-checkpoint license.

parameters_b.note: No total production count was found in the launch, current exact model specification, training guide, later first-party research or later system card. No released weights/configuration permit reconstruction. GPT-4 rumors, other GPT versions and research-feature counts cannot supply this value.

active_parameters_b.note: No activated parameter count or routing specification for this exact full-size model was found in the inspected original and later sources. Do not substitute a total, a sibling count or an assumed dense-model equivalence.

architecture.note: Broad Transformer classification follows the documented inference mechanism and its explicit application to gpt-4.1, whose current alias targets gpt-4.1-2025-04-14. This is operational evidence, not a dedicated architecture report: it establishes a Transformer attention stack, but not a complete block inventory, exclusively Transformer layers, dense versus MoE feed-forward routing, or parameter counts. No sibling architecture is transferred.

context_window.note: The exact official specification is 1,047,576 tokens. The launch uses rounded 1M language. Retain the precise documented value; do not substitute 1,048,576 or confuse the separate 32,768 output cap with context.

modalities.note: Native model inputs are text and image, with text output. Keep PDF under the existing catalog convention for supported document input: the exact GPT-4.1 API example accepts a PDF and preprocesses it into text plus page images. No native PDF, audio or video sensory module is inferred.

reasoning.note: Both sources explicitly classify GPT-4.1 as non-reasoning. Prompted visible planning remains possible, but is distinct from a dedicated internal reasoning mode; false is supported directly rather than inferred from silence.

tool_call.note: Official model specification lists function calling and the exact dated snapshot is demonstrated producing function calls in the primary prompting guide.

description.value: Model for text and image understanding, coding, instruction following and long-context tasks.
description.note: Replace the unsubstantiated long-lived workhorse framing with documented inputs and tasks; omit current-best claims and unsupported size or architecture assertions.

patch.description: Model for text and image understanding, coding, instruction following and long-context tasks.
patch.notes: The gpt-4.1 alias defaults to gpt-4.1-2025-04-14, released in the API on April 14, 2025. Exact documented context is 1,047,576 tokens. PDF input is processed into text and page images. GPT-4.1 has no dedicated internal reasoning mode, but supports prompted visible planning and function calling. Transformer attention is documented; dense/MoE routing and total/active parameter counts remain undisclosed. Deprecated October 14, 2026; API shutdown is scheduled for January 14, 2027, not already completed at review time.

summary: Reviewed all 14 fields. Confirms April 14, 2025 API release, exact 1,047,576-token context, text/image/PDF input, text output, non-reasoning classification and function calling. Adds specific GPT-4.1 family and proprietary classification, replaces marketing copy and records the alias target and scheduled retirement. Later first-party caching documentation establishes broad Transformer architecture. Dense/MoE routing and counts remain undisclosed.
